summary:
Earth Detective is an interactive web application that makes NASA Earth science data accessible to everyone, especially children and people without scientific backgrounds.

Our project addresses NASA's "Be an Earth System Trend Detective" challenge by allowing users to explore how environmental conditions change over time in different locations around the world.

Using real data from NASA POWER, Earth Detective analyzes temperature, humidity, and wind speed through statistical methods, including linear regression and significance testing. Rather than overwhelming users with complicated graphs and statistical terminology, the application transforms its findings into understandable explanations and interactive visualizations.

Our goal is to encourage curiosity about our planet, improve environmental awareness, and make scientific information more accessible. By helping people investigate changes in their own communities, Earth Detective makes Earth science relevant to everyday life.
details:
How does Earth Detective work?

Earth Detective allows users to investigate environmental changes in their own communities using NASA Earth science data.

Users begin by selecting a location, choosing an environmental variable such as temperature, relative humidity, or wind speed, and specifying a time period. They can select a city, enter custom coordinates, or optionally use their approximate location.

Our Python backend retrieves monthly environmental data through the NASA POWER API, processes the measurements into annual averages, and applies Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) linear regression to identify long-term trends.

We calculate the rate of change, coefficient of determination (R²), and statistical significance using a Student's t-test and 95% confidence interval.

Instead of presenting these complicated statistical results directly, Earth Detective translates them into simple explanations. For example, users can discover whether their region has become warmer over time, approximately how much the temperature has changed, and how strong the statistical evidence is.

The application also provides interactive yearly and monthly charts, allowing users to explore the original measurements and observe how conditions vary over time.

For users interested in the mathematics, an optional section reveals the underlying statistical calculations and scientific limitations.

Technologies and tools

Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript, and custom SVG visualizations. The responsive interface is designed to work across desktop and mobile devices.

Backend: Python and FastAPI, with NumPy and SciPy supporting mathematical calculations. We manually implemented the core linear regression formulas rather than relying on prebuilt regression algorithms.

Data: NASA POWER's monthly meteorological data, primarily derived from NASA's MERRA-2 atmospheric reanalysis produced by the Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO).

Development: Visual Studio Code, Python testing tools, and AI-assisted development.

Creativity and accessibility

Our main innovation is combining scientific statistical analysis with child-friendly environmental storytelling.

Many scientific platforms provide powerful datasets and complex visualizations but require technical knowledge to interpret their findings. Earth Detective bridges this gap by separating the scientific analysis from the way results are communicated.

The backend performs the mathematical calculations, while a dedicated interpretation layer transforms the findings into clear, accessible explanations.

Our design prioritizes simplicity, curiosity, and accessibility while keeping the scientific information available for more advanced users.

Intended impact

Earth Detective aims to make Earth science understandable, engaging, and accessible to a wider audience.

By enabling users to explore how their local environment has changed over time, we hope to encourage scientific curiosity, strengthen data literacy, and help communities better understand the environmental changes taking place around them.

Our ultimate vision is to make everyone capable of becoming an Earth Detective, regardless of their age or scientific background.
